questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
questions.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{x}^{2}+3\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{2}+3)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(8x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8(x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D) \\  & =-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=8D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={[-(4{x}^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+8x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+8\operatorname{cos}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(-(4{\pi }^{2}+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +8\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +8\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )-(-3\operatorname{cos}⁡0+8(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡0+8\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =(4{\pi }^{2}+3-8)-(-3+8) \\  & =4{\pi }^{2}-5-5 \\  & =4{\pi }^{2}-10\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10(x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D) \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=10D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={[-(5{x}^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(-(5{\pi }^{2}+7)\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +10\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +10\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )-(-7\operatorname{cos}⁡0+10(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡0+10\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =(5{\pi }^{2}+7-10)-(-7+10) \\  & =5{\pi }^{2}-3-3 \\  & =5{\pi }^{2}-6\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=12x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(6{x}^{2})(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(12x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =6{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-12\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =6{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-12\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =6{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-12(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x+D) \\  & =6{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+12x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-12\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-12D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}6{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={[6{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+12x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-12\operatorname{sin}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =(\frac{3{\pi }^{2}}{2}-12)-0 \\  & =\frac{3{\pi }^{2}}{2}-12\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of a Logarithmic Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
questions.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{1}^{e}({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡(4)}(${{field-1}}$)$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{4}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 1\,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2{log}_{4}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int {log}_{4}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{4}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 1\,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{4}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{4}⁡x)(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{4}⁡x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{4}⁡x-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(x{log}_{4}⁡x-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{4}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2x{log}_{4}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}+C \\  & =\frac{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}-\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}({ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}.$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{4}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}({log}_{4}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}({ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2)]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}({ln}^{2}⁡e-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+2)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}({ln}^{2}⁡1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+2) \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}(1-2+2)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}(0-0+2) \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}-\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡4} \\  & =\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡4}(\,e-2\,)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}2({log}_{3}⁡(2x))^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡(3)}(${{field-1}}$)$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{3}⁡(2x))^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=2\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 2\,\text{d}x=2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2({log}_{3}⁡(2x))^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{3}⁡(2x))}^{2}(2x)-\int (2x)(\frac{2{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x{({log}_{3}⁡(2x))}^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 1\,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡(2x))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2({log}_{3}⁡(2x))^{2}\,\text{d}x & =2x{({log}_{3}⁡(2x))}^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x{log}_{3}⁡(2x)-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =2x{({log}_{3}⁡(2x))}^{2}-\frac{4x{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{4x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{2x{ln}^{2}⁡(2x)}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+\frac{4x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡(2x)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+4)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{4D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡(2x)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}2({log}_{3}⁡(2x))^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡(2x)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+4)]}_{1/2}^{e/2} \\  & =\frac{e/2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡e-4\operatorname{ln}⁡e+4)-\frac{1/2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2{ln}^{2}⁡1-4\operatorname{ln}⁡1+4) \\  & =\frac{e/2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(2-4+4)-\frac{1/2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(0-0+4) \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡3} \\  & =\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(\,e-2\,)\end{aligned}
$$
